page: Vultr vc2-1c-1gb is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 1 shared vCPU based on x86_64 Intel architecture clocked at 2.0 GHz, paired with 1.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes 25 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are present on this server configuration.

Benchmark data situates the computational and throughput capabilities of this instance in the bottom decile across tested categories. The single shared vCPU achieved a PassMark CPU score of 1061.65 and a stress-ng multi-core and single-core score of 691.39. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 67.6 GB/sec for small cached blocks (16 KB), declining to 7.8 GB/sec for large uncached reads (256 MB) and 5.19 GB/sec for writes. The PassMark database operations metric reached 488.23, while Redis SET performance hit 1.0 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reached 0.95 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs focus primarily on resource contention and memory density. The 1:1 ratio between vCPU count and RAM limits parallel tasks and memory-intensive processes. Furthermore, the shared core model exposes tasks to potential multi-tenant contention, making throughput unsuitable for compute-heavy batch workloads or large database indexing. However, the bundling of 25 GB NVMe SSD storage provides low-latency local disk access compared to standard virtualized block storage.

This server is qualitatively cost-effective for basic baseline needs requiring minimal compute footprint. It functions best for entry-level workloads including lightweight web servers, low-traffic static site hosting, basic automation scripts, development sandboxes, and minimal network edge nodes.
